paragraphs: Children in care from Preston are looked after by Lancashire County Council, whose fostering service is run from County Hall in the city, and by the independent agencies and charities listed on this page. The council's information pack says it fosters children from birth to 18 and has a particular need for carers who can take older children and larger groups of brothers and sisters, so that siblings can stay together. It also places parents with their babies through parent and child fostering.

To apply to the council you need to be over 21, have a spare bedroom for the child's sole use and have lived in the UK for at least the last six months. You can be single or married, rent or own your home, and work or be at home full-time. Smokers can foster children aged five and over. The council says assessment usually takes four to six months, and new carers attend a three-day Skills to Foster course at County Hall in Preston.

Lancashire pays a weekly allowance for each child, plus welcome, holiday, birthday and festival payments, with enhanced packages for parent and child placements, disabled children, children with complex needs and sibling groups. The pack does not publish the figures, so ask for them. Support includes a named social worker, a 24-hour phone line, a mentor who is an experienced foster carer, support groups and a wellbeing programme, and the council says Ofsted rates its children's services Good.

Because agencies set their own fees, training and support, it is worth speaking to the council and two or three of the services below before you decide, and asking each what they pay and how they help out of hours.

sources.title: Foster carers share highlights of rewarding, happy vocation (Lancashire County Council, 12 August 2024)
